title: Minuta 2025-07-29
summary: The minutes of the July meeting show a Council fully aligned on easing: all five members agreed that the latest data validated the June IPoM path of a gradual reduction of the TPM toward its neutral range, and that the only plausible option was a 25bp cut to 4.75%, voted by Costa, Novy, Naudon, Cespedes and Soto. The June CPI miss is attributed to volatile items expected to reverse, convergence to 3% is still seen in the first half of 2026 with a practically closed output gap, and the points of attention are wage costs and their inflation effects plus external risks (a possibly tighter Fed and adverse financial conditions for EMs). Versus the June minutes, where the Council weighed holding at 5% against cutting and chose to wait mainly for tactical-communication reasons and the Middle East uncertainty, the option set has collapsed to a single cut and the debate is about pace rather than direction. The minutes read in line with the communique of the same meeting, neither more dovish nor more hawkish: the gradual-easing guidance is confirmed without any hint of acceleration.

key_quotes.quote: Todos los Consejeros concordaron en que estos antecedentes validaban la trayectoria de política monetaria contenida en el último IPoM, donde se contemplaba una reducción gradual de la TPM hacia su rango neutral en los próximos trimestres.
key_quotes.context: Unanimous endorsement of the gradual easing path

key_quotes.quote: todos los Consejeros coincidieron en que la única opción plausible era reducir la TPM en 25 puntos base
key_quotes.context: Option set narrowed to a single 25bp cut (vs hold-or-cut in June)

key_quotes.quote: En particular, la evolución del mercado laboral y cómo los mayores costos salariales afectarían tanto el empleo como el ingreso de los trabajadores, y cuáles serían sus consecuencias para la dinámica inflacionaria.
key_quotes.context: Wage costs flagged as a point to monitor

key_quotes.quote: Así, en el escenario más probable, la actividad económica se mantendría en torno a su tendencia, con una brecha prácticamente cerrada, y la inflación convergería al 3% en la primera mitad de 2026.
key_quotes.context: Central scenario: closed gap, convergence by 1H26
